questions.stem: A sum of money becomes Rs. \(15,000\) in \(2\) years and Rs. \(18,000\) in \(3\) years when invested at compound interest. What is the principal amount?
questions.keySolution:
Let principal be \(P\) and rate be \(R\)%.
Given \(\frac{18000}{15000}=1.2\Rightarrow 1+\frac{R}{100}=1.2\Rightarrow R=20\)%.
\(P\times(1.2)^2=15000\Rightarrow P=\frac{15000}{1.44}=Rs.\,10,416.67\).

questions.keySolution:
Let \(P\) be principal.
\(P[(1.15)^2-1]=1935\Rightarrow P=\frac{1935}{0.3225}=6000\).
Simple interest \(=\frac{6000\times15\times2}{100}=Rs.\,1,800\).

The compound interest on a sum for \(2\) years is Rs. \(832\) and the simple interest for the same period is Rs. \(800\). Find the principal.
questions.keySolution:
Let \(P\), rate \(R\)%.  Difference \(CI-SI=P(R/100)^2=32\).  Also \(SI=\frac{PR\times2}{100}=800\Rightarrow PR=40000\).
\(P(\frac{R}{100})=400\) and \(P(\frac{R}{100})^2=32\Rightarrow400\times\frac{R}{100}=32\Rightarrow\frac{R}{100}=0.08\Rightarrow R=8\)%.
\(P=\frac{400}{0.08}=Rs.\,5,000\).

questions.stem: A sum lent for \(2\) years at \(20\)% compound interest would earn Rs. \(482\) more if interest is compounded half-yearly instead of annually. Find the sum.
questions.keySolution:
Annual amount factor \(=1.2^2=1.44\).
Half-yearly factor \(=(1.1)^4=1.4641\).
Difference \(=0.0241P=482\Rightarrow P=\frac{482}{0.0241}=Rs.\,20,000\).
